healthy_wheat.immediate_steps: Monitor the plant regularly and keep leaves dry where possible.
healthy_wheat.treatment: No treatment needed. Keep balanced watering and feeding, and remove any dead leaves promptly.
healthy_wheat.prevention: Give good air circulation, avoid overwatering, and check leaves weekly so any new problem is caught early.
healthy_wheat.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.

wheat_brown_rust.immediate_steps: Remove infected leaves, improve air circulation, and avoid wetting leaves when watering.
wheat_brown_rust.treatment: A triazole fungicide such as propiconazole (Tilt) or tebuconazole (Folicur), or azoxystrobin + difenoconazole (Amistar Top), labelled for wheat leaf rust, may help — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice. Apply at the first sign of rust pustules.
wheat_brown_rust.prevention: Water at the base, space plants for airflow, rotate crops, and clean up fallen leaves.
wheat_brown_rust.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
wheat_brown_rust.source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad — wheat rust control recommendations; AARI trial, cv. Akbar-19

wheat_septoria.immediate_steps: Remove affected leaves, avoid excess nitrogen, and spray at early flag-leaf emergence if the disease is spreading.
wheat_septoria.treatment: A triazole fungicide such as propiconazole or tebuconazole, labelled for wheat Septoria leaf blotch, may help — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice. Spray at early flag-leaf emergence, before the disease reaches the flag leaf.
wheat_septoria.prevention: Use resistant varieties where available, avoid excess nitrogen, rotate crops, and bury or remove infected stubble.
wheat_septoria.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
wheat_septoria.source: Pacific Northwest Plant Disease Management Handbook (rev. Mar 2026) — Wheat Septoria Tritici Blotch; Agriculture Victoria — Septoria Tritici Blotch of Wheat

wheat_yellow_rust.immediate_steps: Remove severely infected leaves, improve air circulation, and avoid wetting leaves when watering. Check the flag leaf first, as it matters most for yield.
wheat_yellow_rust.treatment: A fungicide labelled for wheat yellow rust may help — for example propiconazole or tebuconazole, or azoxystrobin + difenoconazole (Amistar Top), always following the product label and local agricultural advice. Apply at the first sign of yellow stripes.
wheat_yellow_rust.prevention: Use rust-resistant wheat varieties where available, avoid late sowing, scout weekly in early spring, and remove volunteer wheat plants.
wheat_yellow_rust.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
wheat_yellow_rust.source: Ayub Agricultural Research Institute (AARI), Faisalabad — wheat rust control recommendations; ICAR — stripe rust trial

wheat_black_rust.immediate_steps: Scout the crop at once, especially stems and flag leaves, and spray at the first sign of pustules — black rust spreads fast in warm, humid weather.
wheat_black_rust.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
wheat_black_rust.prevention: Sow resistant varieties, remove volunteer wheat and barberry near fields, avoid late sowing, and rotate crops.
wheat_black_rust.treatment: A triazole fungicide such as propiconazole or tebuconazole, or a strobilurin mix such as azoxystrobin + difenoconazole, labelled for wheat stem rust, may help — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice. Resistant varieties are the main defence.
wheat_black_rust.source: CABI Plantwise Plus Knowledge Bank — stem rust PMDG; FAO AGRIS stem-rust fungicide trial

wheat_powdery_mildew.immediate_steps: Remove heavily infected leaves, improve airflow through the crop, and spray at the first sign of white powdery patches.
wheat_powdery_mildew.note: General guidance only. For chemical use, always follow the product label and local agricultural extension advice.
wheat_powdery_mildew.prevention: Sow resistant varieties, avoid excess nitrogen and dense sowing, space plants for airflow, and rotate crops.
wheat_powdery_mildew.treatment: A triazole fungicide such as propiconazole or tebuconazole, or sulphur, labelled for wheat powdery mildew, may help — always follow the product label and local agricultural advice. Spray soon after the disease appears.
wheat_powdery_mildew.source: Pacific Northwest Plant Disease Management Handbook (rev. Mar 2026) — Wheat Powdery Mildew; Crop Protection Network fungicide efficacy table 2026
